Describe the data for all females

```{r}
NESEdata <- read.csv('../results/All_Clusters.csv')

Sum.All <- describe(NESEdata[,c("d13C","d15N","MaxLat_degrees","MinLon_degrees",
                                "MedianDistToContShelf_km",
                                "SdDistContShelf_km","MesoEcoProportionShelf","MesoEcoProportionCAC",
                      "MesoEcoProportionSubArcticPac","MesoEcoProportionNorthCPac","Mean_Depth_m",
                      "Mean_Depth_sd","Mean_Duration_sec","Mean_Duration_sd","Pct_TransitDives",
                      "Pct_ForagingDives","Pct_DriftDives","Pct_BenthicDives","PctTripDiving",
                      "DeepDayForageDivesMedian_m","DeepNightForageDivesMedian_m")],fast = TRUE)

Sum.Trips <- describeBy(NESEdata[,c("d13C","d15N","MaxLat_degrees","MinLon_degrees",
                                "MedianDistToContShelf_km",
                                "SdDistContShelf_km","MesoEcoProportionShelf","MesoEcoProportionCAC",
                      "MesoEcoProportionSubArcticPac","MesoEcoProportionNorthCPac","Mean_Depth_m",
                      "Mean_Depth_sd","Mean_Duration_sec","Mean_Duration_sd","Pct_TransitDives",
                      "Pct_ForagingDives","Pct_DriftDives","Pct_BenthicDives","PctTripDiving",
                      "DeepDayForageDivesMedian_m","DeepNightForageDivesMedian_m")],
                      group = NESEdata$Trip,
                      fast = TRUE)


```

Test for differences in the variables across the differences groups

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggpubr)
library(rstatix)
library(ggstatsplot)

# Between PB and PM
NESEdata <- read.csv('../results/All_Clusters.csv')
NESEdata$fTrip <- as.factor(NESEdata$Trip)
levels(NESEdata$fTrip)

# d13C
ggboxplot(NESEdata, x = "fTrip", y = "d13C") + 
  ylab(expression(paste(delta^{13},'C (‰)', sep = ''))) +
  xlab('Trip') + 
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c('PostBreeding' = "Post-Breeding", "PostMolt" = "Post-Moult"))


NESEdata %>% 
  group_by(fTrip) %>%
  identify_outliers(d13C)


# Check for normality assumption

# Build the linear model
model  <- lm(d13C ~ fTrip, data = NESEdata)
# Create a QQ plot of residuals
ggqqplot(residuals(model))


# Compute Shapiro-Wilk test of normality
shapiro_test(residuals(model)) # Data are not normally distributed, but because N > 50 it's better to use the qqplot to make a decision

ggqqplot(NESEdata, "d13C", facet.by = "fTrip")

# Use a K-W test
d13C.kw <- NESEdata %>% kruskal_test(d13C ~ fTrip)
d13C.kw

p <- ggbetweenstats(data = NESEdata,
               x = fTrip,
               y = d13C,
               xlab = 'Trip',
               ylab= expression(paste(delta^{13},'C (‰)', sep = '')),
               boxplot.args = list(width = 0), # to remove box plot
               type = "np", 
               conf.level = 0.99,
               package = "ggsci",
               palette = "uniform_startrek")
print(p)

pdf('../figures/Tripd13C.pdf') # saves the figure
print(p)
dev.off()

######################################################
# d15N
ggboxplot(NESEdata, x = "fTrip", y = "d15N") + 
  ylab(expression(paste(delta^{15},'N (‰)', sep = ''))) +
  xlab('Trip') + 
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c('PostBreeding' = "Post-Breeding", "PostMolt" = "Post-Moult"))


NESEdata %>% 
  group_by(fTrip) %>%
  identify_outliers(d15N)

NESEdata %>% 
  group_by(fTrip) %>%
  identify_outliers(d15N)


# Check for normality assumption

# Build the linear model
model  <- lm(d15N ~ fTrip, data = NESEdata)

ggqqplot(residuals(model))

ggqqplot(NESEdata, "d15N", facet.by = "fTrip")

# Use a K-W test
d15N.kw <- NESEdata %>% kruskal_test(d15N ~ fTrip)
d15N.kw

p <- ggbetweenstats(data = NESEdata,
               x = fTrip,
               y = d15N,
               xlab = 'Trip',
               ylab= expression(paste(delta^{15},'N (‰)', sep = '')),
               boxplot.args = list(width = 0), # to remove box plot
               type = "np", 
               conf.level = 0.99,
               package = "ggsci",
               palette = "uniform_startrek")

print(p)

pdf('../figures/Tripd15N.pdf') # saves the figure
print(p)
dev.off()

```

Differences in parameters for PB Clusters
```{r}
# Wihtin PB Clusters
NESEdata <- read.csv('../results/PB_Clusters.csv')
NESEdata$fCluster <- as.factor(NESEdata$cluster)
levels(NESEdata$fCluster)

################################################################################
# d13C
ggboxplot(NESEdata, x = "fCluster", y = "d13C") + 
  ylab(expression(paste(delta^{13},'C (‰)', sep = ''))) +
  xlab('Post-Breeding') 

NESEdata %>% 
  group_by(fCluster) %>%
  identify_outliers(d13C)


# Check for normality assumption

# Build the linear model
model  <- lm(d13C ~ fCluster, data = NESEdata)
# Create a QQ plot of residuals
ggqqplot(residuals(model))


# Compute Shapiro-Wilk test of normality
shapiro_test(residuals(model)) # Data are  normally distributed, but because N > 50 it's better to use the qqplot to make a decision

ggqqplot(NESEdata, "d13C", facet.by = "fCluster")

# Use an ANOVA test
d13C.aov <- NESEdata %>% anova_test(d13C ~ fCluster)
d13C.aov

# Post-hoc
d13C.pwc <- NESEdata %>% tukey_hsd(d13C ~ fCluster)
d13C.pwc

pwc <- d13C.pwc %>% add_xy_position(x = "fCluster")

p <- ggbetweenstats(data = NESEdata,
               x = fCluster,
               y = d13C,
               xlab = 'PB Clusters',
               ylab= expression(paste(delta^{13},'C (‰)', sep = '')),
               boxplot.args = list(width = 0), # to remove box plot
               type = "parametric", 
               conf.level = 0.99,
               package = "ggsci",
               palette = "uniform_startrek") 

  
print(p)

pdf('../figures/PBCluster_d13C.pdf') # saves the figure
print(p)
dev.off()

################################################################################
## d15N
ggboxplot(NESEdata, x = "fCluster", y = "d15N") + 
  ylab(expression(paste(delta^{15},'N (‰)', sep = ''))) +
  xlab('Post-Breeding')

NESEdata %>% 
  group_by(fCluster) %>%
  identify_outliers(d15N)


# Check for normality assumption

# Build the linear model
model  <- lm(d15N ~ fCluster, data = NESEdata)
# Create a QQ plot of residuals
ggqqplot(residuals(model))


# Compute Shapiro-Wilk test of normality
shapiro_test(residuals(model)) # Data are not normally distributed, but because N > 50 it's better to use the qqplot to make a decision

ggqqplot(NESEdata, "d15N", facet.by = "fCluster")

# Use a K-W test
d15N.kw <- NESEdata %>% kruskal_test(d15N ~ fCluster)
d15N.kw

# Posthoc Dunn's test
d15N.pwc <- NESEdata %>% dunn_test(d15N ~ fCluster, p.adjust.method = 'bonferroni')
d15N.pwc

pwc <- d15N.pwc %>% add_xy_position(x = "fCluster")

p <- ggbetweenstats(data = NESEdata,
               x = fCluster,
               y = d15N,
               xlab = 'PB Clusters',
               ylab= expression(paste(delta^{15},'N (‰)', sep = '')),
               boxplot.args = list(width = 0), # to remove box plot
               type = "np", 
               conf.level = 0.99,
               package = "ggsci",
               palette = "uniform_startrek") 
  
print(p)

pdf('../figures/PBCluster_d15N.pdf') # saves the figure
print(p)
dev.off()

```

# Compute Shapiro-Wilk test of normality
shapiro_test(residuals(model)) # Data are not normally distributed, but because N > 50 it's better to use the qqplot to make a decision

MesoEcoProportionCAC.kw

# Dunn's test

                                                 p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")

               y = MesoEcoProportionCAC,

               package = "ggsci",
               palette = "uniform_startrek")

Differences in parameters for PM Clusters
```{r}
# Within PM Clusters
NESEdata <- read.csv('../results/PM_Clusters.csv')
NESEdata$fCluster <- as.factor(NESEdata$cluster)
levels(NESEdata$fCluster)

################################################################################
# d13C
ggboxplot(NESEdata, x = "fCluster", y = "d13C") + 
  ylab(expression(paste(delta^{13},'C (‰)', sep = ''))) +
  xlab('Post-Moult') 

NESEdata %>% 
  group_by(fCluster) %>%
  identify_outliers(d13C)


# Check for normality assumption

# Build the linear model
model  <- lm(d13C ~ fCluster, data = NESEdata)
# Create a QQ plot of residuals
ggqqplot(residuals(model))


# Compute Shapiro-Wilk test of normality
shapiro_test(residuals(model)) # Data are  normally distributed, but because N > 50 it's better to use the qqplot to make a decision

ggqqplot(NESEdata, "d13C", facet.by = "fCluster")

# Use an ANOVA test
d13C.aov <- NESEdata %>% anova_test(d13C ~ fCluster)
d13C.aov

# Post-hoc
d13C.pwc <- NESEdata %>% tukey_hsd(d13C ~ fCluster)
d13C.pwc

pwc <- d13C.pwc %>% add_xy_position(x = "fCluster")

p <- ggbetweenstats(data = NESEdata,
               x = fCluster,
               y = d13C,
               xlab = 'PM Clusters',
               ylab= expression(paste(delta^{13},'C (‰)', sep = '')),
               boxplot.args = list(width = 0), # to remove box plot
               type = "parametric", 
               conf.level = 0.99,
               package = "ggsci",
               palette = "uniform_startrek")
  
print(p)

pdf('../figures/PMCluster_d13C.pdf') # saves the figure
print(p)
dev.off()

################################################################################
## d15N
ggboxplot(NESEdata, x = "fCluster", y = "d15N") + 
  ylab(expression(paste(delta^{15},'N (‰)', sep = ''))) +
  xlab('Post-Moult')

NESEdata %>% 
  group_by(fCluster) %>%
  identify_outliers(d15N)


# Check for normality assumption

# Build the linear model
model  <- lm(d15N ~ fCluster, data = NESEdata)
# Create a QQ plot of residuals
ggqqplot(residuals(model))


# Compute Shapiro-Wilk test of normality
shapiro_test(residuals(model)) # Data are not normally distributed, but because N > 50 it's better to use the qqplot to make a decision

ggqqplot(NESEdata, "d15N", facet.by = "fCluster")

# Use a K-W test
d15N.kw <- NESEdata %>% kruskal_test(d15N ~ fCluster)
d15N.kw

# Posthoc Dunn's test
d15N.pwc <- NESEdata %>% dunn_test(d15N ~ fCluster, p.adjust.method = 'bonferroni')
d15N.pwc

pwc <- d15N.pwc %>% add_xy_position(x = "fCluster")

p <- ggbetweenstats(data = NESEdata,
               x = fCluster,
               y = d15N,
               xlab = 'PM Clusters',
               ylab= expression(paste(delta^{15},'N (‰)', sep = '')),
               boxplot.args = list(width = 0), # to remove box plot
               type = "np", 
               conf.level = 0.99,
               package = "ggsci",
               palette = "uniform_startrek")
  
print(p)

pdf('../figures/PMCluster_d15N.pdf') # saves the figure
print(p)
dev.off()

```

ggboxplot(NESEdata, x = "fCluster", y = "Pct_TransitDives") + 
  ylab("Percentage transit Dives (%)") +
  xlab('Post-Moult')

NESEdata %>% 
  group_by(fCluster) %>%
  identify_outliers(Pct_TransitDives)


# Check for normality assumption
# Build the linear model
model  <- lm(Pct_TransitDives ~ fCluster, data = NESEdata)
# Create a QQ plot of residuals
ggqqplot(residuals(model))


# Compute Shapiro-Wilk test of normality
shapiro_test(residuals(model)) # Data are not normally distributed, but because N > 50 it's better to use the qqplot to make a decision

ggqqplot(NESEdata, "Pct_TransitDives", facet.by = "fCluster")

# Use an ANOVA K-W test
Pct_TransitDives.aov <- NESEdata %>% anova_test(Pct_TransitDives ~ fCluster)
Pct_TransitDives.aov

# Tukey's test
Pct_TransitDives.pwc <- NESEdata %>% tukey_hsd(Pct_TransitDives ~ fCluster)


pwc <- Pct_TransitDives.pwc  %>% add_xy_position(x = "fCluster")

p <- ggbetweenstats(data = NESEdata,
               x = fCluster,
               y = Pct_TransitDives,
               xlab = 'PM Clusters',
               ylab= 'Percentage Transit Dives (%)',
               boxplot.args = list(width = 0), # to remove box plot
               type = "parametric", 
               conf.level = 0.99,
               package = "ggsci",
               palette = "uniform_startrek")
  
print(p)

pdf('../figures/PMCluster_Pct_TransitDives.pdf') # saves the figure
print(p)
dev.off()
